note: Access International Financial Services, securities processing software for brokers. Level 8 Systems took its stock for consulting work in 2000 and 2001 and sold that interest on 2001-10-01, and the company's contract suit against Level 8 in the District of Colorado settled in February 2003 (Level 8 10-K for 2002); nothing later was found, so its fate is not established. No round named; 2002 is the first year the firm listed it, not an investment year.

Billing mediation software for IP services over broadband networks. K2 Digital's annual report names AP Engines, Inc. among its five largest clients of 2000; EDGAR full text, Light Reading and Google News (searched 2026-10-06) show nothing later, so its fate is not established. No round named; 2000 is the firm's own investment year.

Traffic management chips for optical networks, Sunnyvale. The company's release of 2002-03-11 says 'Series A investors Bessemer Venture Partners, Highland Capital Partners, and Commonwealth Capital Ventures co-led' the $19M Series B and that it 'raised $10 million from its first round of funding in 2000', so the entry is the 2000 Series A. Acq. by Cortina Systems, 2005 (Light Reading, 2005-02-02).

funding_rounds.lead: Bessemer Venture Partners; Highland Capital Partners; Commonwealth Capital Ventures

note: Chinese blog host Bokee (bokee.com, formerly BlogChina), Beijing. Wikipedia (Fang Xingdong) says it 'received some funding from venture capital firms in 2005' without naming the round, and the firm first listed it in January 2006, so the stage is undetermined and the date is that funding year. bokee.com still serves a site (read 2026-10-06, its newest notice dated 2020), so it reads private.

Long-haul optical systems maker, Ottawa (formerly Solinet Systems). Bessemer's Rob Soni was already a director when the $93M second round closed on 2001-05-31 with $108M raised in all (company release), so the entry is the unnamed first round of about $15M; the date is the year the company started, inferred, since that round is undated. Closed in August 2003 (Light Reading, 2003-08-05).

Web-based print procurement software for the printing industry. Internet Capital Group held 8% at the end of 2000 and reported no stake at 2001-06-30, and its chief financial officer left in June 2001 (FiberMark proxy, 2002); no source read says whether it was sold or closed, so its fate is not established. No round named; 1998 is the firm's own investment year.

Metro optical equipment maker, Boxborough, Massachusetts. Its release of 2000-06-12 says it 'secured first-round funding from Bessemer Venture Partners, New Enterprise Associates and Columbia Capital', which names no series, so the stage is undetermined; the date is the year of that release, the round itself is undated (the company was founded in 1999). Closed on 2004-01-20 (Light Reading, 2004-01-21).

Memory firewall security software, Redwood City; first listed by the firm in April 2004 under its earlier name Araksha. VMware's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2007-09-30 says it 'acquired Determina, Inc.' in that quarter: acq. by VMware, 2007. No round named; 2004 is the first year the firm listed it, not an investment year.

Online steel marketplace e-STEEL, New York, renamed NewView Technologies in 2001: the firm's own 2002 listing reads 'NewView Technologies (formerly e-STEEL Corporation)', so this row and newview-technologies are one company. It was still a privately held software company in February 2003 (a former officer's biography in a Citizens Communications 10-K) and nothing later was found, so its fate is not established; the Greylock book's two rows read acquired and defunct from memory. No round named; 1998 is the firm's own investment year.

Security policy compliance software co-founded by Dan Farmer, San Mateo (city from memory). Its site still serves as Elemental Cyber Security, Inc. (read 2026-10-06, copyright 2021), fresher than the Sequoia book's uncited defunct reading, so it reads private. No round named; 2004 is the first year the firm listed it, not an investment year.

Exchange platform software for online markets. Its former president and chief executive Timothy Campbell took over Industri-Matematik from January 2003 (that company's release of 2002-12-19); no source read says what became of ePIT, so its fate is not established. No round named; 2000 is the firm's own investment year.

Tools and templates that extend ERP applications (Exemplary Software). Business Objects' proxies of 2002 and 2003 still list a director's seat at Exemplary Software and the firm listed it until 2005; nothing later was found, so its fate is not established. No round named; 1998 is the firm's own investment year.

CRM consulting, systems integration and training services (The Extraprise Group), Boston (city from memory). The firm listed it until 2005; its domain now serves an unrelated gambling page (read 2026-10-06) and no source read reports a sale or a closure, so its fate is not established. No round named; 1997 is the firm's own investment year.

basis: The firm's own history page (bvp.com/port/onepage.asp, Common Crawl capture of 2008-11-20): 'Pete Bancroft joined Bessemer in 1967 to lead the venture practice. Some of his signature deals were Measurex, Fotomat, and Interdata.' A deal of the venture group before the 1981 spin-out, stated on the firm's own site (decisions.md R2, X1).

note: Drive-up photo finishing kiosks, founded in San Diego with the first kiosk in 1965; public in 1971 and acq. by Konishiroku (Konica), 1986 (Wikipedia). The firm's history page names it a signature deal of Pete Bancroft, who joined in 1967; no source read dates the investment or names the round, so the stage is undetermined and the entry undated.

basis: Fortune (2026-05-14) on the company's $5 million pre-seed: 'Silent Ventures led the round with participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, SV Angel, Vanderbilt University, Channel 39 Ventures, and the founders of companies including Anduril and Armada.'

note: Maker of low-cost interceptor missiles, Los Angeles. Fortune (2026-05-14) reports the $5 million pre-seed led by Silent Ventures with Bessemer participating, the entry. TechCrunch (2026-10-06) reports a $25 million seed led by Benchmark at a $125 million valuation 'according to a person familiar with the company', the newest round found (Google News, 2026-10-06), far below $1B.

Online cosmetics retailer, San Francisco (city from memory). Estee Lauder's 10-K for fiscal 2001: in fiscal 2000 'We also acquired Gloss.com, an Internet beauty site': acq. by Estee Lauder, 2000. No round named; 1999 is the firm's own investment year.

basis: Perion's release in its Form 6-K (2014-06-30): 'Grow Mobile is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York and is venture-backed by Signia Venture Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners.'

note: Mobile app advertising platform, San Francisco, 'founded less than two years ago' in June 2014. Acq. by Perion Network, 2014 (definitive agreement announced 2014-06-30, Perion's 6-K). The record read names Bessemer only as a backer, with no round and no date (Google News searched 2026-10-06), so the stage is undetermined and the entry undated.

Direct marketing and web commerce service on the firm's 2000 listing. The only later trace is a Zeta Global 10-K naming an executive's earlier work at the startup Hotsocket; no source read says what became of it, so its fate is not established. No round named; 2000 is the firm's own investment year.

Billing reconciliation software for telecommunications carriers. Its chairman's term ran from April 1995 to June 2000 (Performance Technologies proxy, 2001) and nothing later was found, so its fate is not established. No round named; 1995 is the firm's own investment year.

Broadband gateway chips and software, Santa Clara. Philips bought a 51 percent interest for $25 million in February 2002, and in August 2003 the company was still run independently and rebuilding after losing its Bangalore unit (Light Reading); nothing later was found, so its fate is not established. No round named; 1999 is the firm's own investment year.

funding_rounds.round: equity investment for a 51 percent interest

note: Transmission lasers for fiber-optic networks, Sunnyvale. The company's release of 2001-03-14 says Bessemer 'headed' the $29 million second round and lists the 'first-round financing participants' separately without it, so the entry is the second round, which reads Growth. Acq. by Emcore, 2006 (merger closed 2006-01-12, Emcore's release).

Cable, telephone and internet provider in the Southeast, West Point, Georgia. Knology's 2002 offering circular lists Bessemer Venture Partners V and Bessec Ventures V among the 'Series B Investors' and dates that private placement to 2000-02-07 ($4.75 a share, about $100.6M); both funds signed the January 2001 amendment to the stockholders agreement of that date (8-K). The entry is the Series B, which reads Growth. Acq. by WideOpenWest, 2012 (Wikipedia).
